question: Your Next app on app.example.com calls Nest on api.example.com with cookie auth. Users see CORS errors and you worry about CSRF. What is your design?
questionBn: app.example.com-এর Next অ্যাপ কুকি অথসহ api.example.com-এর Nestকে কল করে। CORS এরর ও CSRF নিয়ে ডিজাইন কী হবে?
shortAnswer: Allowlist origins with credentials, never use `*` with cookies, and add CSRF defenses for state-changing cookie-authenticated requests—or avoid cross-site cookies via a BFF.
strongAnswer: Prefer a same-site BFF to reduce credentialed CORS. If cross-origin is required: explicit ACAO + ACAC true, SameSite cookie strategy, and CSRF tokens or Fetch Metadata checks on mutating routes. Explain that CORS is browser-enforced and not authorization. Document local vs prod origin allowlists.
advancedAnswer: Discuss partitioned cookies, trusted types, and aligning mobile bearer-token clients that bypass CORS.
followUps: How do Playwright tests handle CSRF tokens?
commonWrongAnswer: Disable CORS entirely or reflect any Origin with credentials.
productionRelevance: Split front/API domains are common and frequently misconfigured under delivery pressure.
integrationProcedure: 1) List browser clients and their origins. 2) Configure CORS allowlist (no * with credentials). 3) If cookies: add CSRF tokens or SameSite=strict/lax appropriately. 4) Test from disallowed origin. 5) Document non-browser clients separately (API keys/mTLS).
